text:
prod_bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 2189991234 - Streaming endpoints: p99 latency breach in us-west-2. p99=1.24s (SLO 500ms). p95 trending up. Automated triage flagged increased backend errors and streaming stalls. Link: https://console.redwood/inci/2189991234

arnold_oncall: ack — I'm on it. starting timeline and pinging SRE/runtime. root cause guess: cache-related? seeing a lot of 503-ish timeouts in frontend logs.

maya_sre: grabbing metrics now. KV prefix-hit rate on cache-cluster-b dropped sharply ~18:16 UTC. before: 84% hit => now: 11%. Eviction rate spiked. p50 unaffected, p95/p99 impacted. streaming tail tokens show repeated fetches for the same prefixes.

jake_runtime: thanks @maya_sre — I just checked deploy history. We rolled out a prefix-hash tweak (optimize-shard-rotation) at 18:10 in canary and promoted at 18:14. Could be hash bucketing change causing namespace churn.

arnold_oncall: ok do we need to rollback the rollout? What's risk to traffic?

jake_runtime: recommend rollback to previous hash mapping immediately for canary and prod. Steps:
1) revert flag: `rdwctl flags set optimize-shard-rotation false --env=prod`
2) restart distributor on affected pools to pick up mapping
3) monitor cache hit rate and streaming tail

maya_sre: while rollback is in flight, let's mitigate with live prefilling: enable aggressive prefetch for top prefixes on node group kv-7 to reduce cold misses. Command:```bash
rdwctl prefetch --cluster cache-cluster-b --prefixes-file /tmp/top-prefixes.txt --mode aggressive
```

arnold_oncall: executing rollback now (step 1) — running command and will paste output.

arnold_oncall: ```bash
$ rdwctl flags set optimize-shard-rotation false --env=prod
OK: flag updated (propagating)
Propagation started 18:22:31 UTC
```

prod_bot: FLAG_CHANGE: optimize-shard-rotation=false applied to env=prod by arnold_oncall. Propagation status: in-progress.

jake_runtime: propagation looks good. kicking graceful restart for distributors on pools a,b,c (non-disruptive):```bash
for s in dist-a dist-b dist-c; do rdwctl service restart $s --graceful; done
```

nico_infra: heads-up — warm restarts will rehydrate some caches, expect a transient CPU bump on distributors. Watching autoscaler.

maya_sre: watching cache metrics — prefetch started at 18:24:10. initial effect: hit rate on kv-shard-7 moved from 11% -> 28% within 90s. p95 improving from ~600ms -> ~380ms in preliminary graphs. p99 still elevated at ~900ms.

liu_cs: getting customer vibes — CS dashboard shows 2 customers with degraded streaming sessions (session dropouts, slower streams). Not yet a widespread error rate but some interactive features are lagging. Flagging for potential SE outreach.

arnold_oncall: post-rollback metrics at 18:28:40: cache global hit-rate now 67% (was 84 pre-incident), kv-shard-7 61% after warmup. p99 dropped to 420ms. Looks like rollback + prefetch mitigated major tail.

prod_bot: SLO_STATUS: p99 0.42s (target 0.5s) — OK. p95 0.16s. Incident severity downgraded to SEV3.

jake_runtime: we should follow-up with a postmortem: quick notes: cause = prefix-hash mapping change increased key dispersion causing cold misses + eviction storms; mitigation = immediate flag rollback, distributor graceful restarts, targeted prefetch for hot prefixes; long-term: add canary traffic shaping, validate hash-mapping with simulated key distribution, and add alert for sudden hit-rate delta >30% within 5m.

maya_sre: adding probe to detect streaming stall signature: repeated KV GETs for identical prefix within 200ms window > 50 => alert. Also capture sample keys for offline analysis.

liu_cs: I'll draft customer comms for the two affected accounts. No data loss, performance blips only. ETA for a status note ~30m.

arnold_oncall: handing off to night oncall @jake_runtime for follow-up and postmortem. Current status: recovery complete, monitoring tight. Last action: enabled retention of sample traces for 2h.

jake_runtime: taking handoff. I'll own the follow-up and PM with infra to change rollout process. Leaving runbook note: https://playbooks.redwood/cache-rollout. Add timeline and metrics snapshots.

nico_infra: I'll work with infra to throttle canary promote by request and ensure flag propagation checks include hit-rate stability.

maya_sre: final metrics snapshot at 18:44 UTC attached to thread (graphs auto-uploaded). p99 stable at ~390-430ms for 30m. Marking incident resolved but will keep in watch for 2 hours.

arnold_oncall: :thumbsup: Good job team. Closing live mitigation. Next steps: postmortem doc, action items assigned to runtime/infra, and a probe added by SRE.

prod_bot: INCIDENT_RESOLVED: 2189991234 — mitigation complete, severity = SEV3. Automated follow-up reminders scheduled for postmortem in 24h.
